Rashi on Nedarim 51b:1:1.hebrew: אינו אסור אלא בכבוש של ירק - דסתם כבוש ירק הוא, אבל אמר כבוש שאני טועם, הואיל ואמר כי האי לישנא, אסור בכל הכבושין, וה"ה בכל הנך. אם אמר בשלוק סתם, אינו אסור כו', דסתם שלוק שלהן אינו אלא בשר, ודעתיה לא הוי אלא בשר, דדרכו להתבשל ולהשלק:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:1:1.english: He is prohibited only from pickled vegetables - For unspecified "pickled food" is [understood as] vegetables; but [if] he said, "pickled food that I taste," since he used such phrasing, he is prohibited from all pickled foods, and the same applies to all these [cases]. If he said "boiled food" without specification, he is not prohibited [except from boiled meat], etc., for their unspecified "boiled food" is nothing other than meat, and his intention was only for meat, as it is normally cooked and boiled.

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:2:1.hebrew: אמר קונם דכביש עלי או דשליק עלי מאי - מי אמרינן דכביש דמי כמ"ד הכבוש, או דילמא דמי כמאן דאמר כבוש שאני טועם, ואסור בכל הכבושין:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:2:1.english: [If] he said, "Konam, that which is pickled [be] upon me," or "that which is boiled [be] upon me," what [is the law]? - Do we say [that] "that which is pickled" is like one who says "the pickled [food]," or perhaps it is like one who says "pickled [food] that I taste," and he is prohibited from all pickled [foods]?

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:2:2.english: Tibe'i [The dilemma remains] - That is to say, teiku [let it stand unresolved].

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:4:1.hebrew: דג דגים שאני טועם - דג משמע גדול, דגים משמע קטנים, וכיון דאמר שניהם, אסור בהן בין גדולים בין קטנים:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:4:1.english: Fish [or] fishes that I taste - "Fish" implies a large [fish], "fishes" implies small [fish], and since he said both of them, he is prohibited from [eating] them, whether large or small.

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:4:2.hebrew: ומותר בטרית טרופה - דג ששמו טרית ומוכרין אותו בחתיכות, שלא נדר אלא מדג הנמכר שלם:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:4:2.english: And he is permitted [to eat] minced tarit - [This is] a fish whose name is tarit, and they sell it in pieces, for he only vowed [to abstain] from fish that is sold whole.

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:4:3.hebrew: ובציר - שעושין מקרבי דגים, וכל שכן במורייס, שאין עושין אותו אלא משומן של דגים:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:4:3.english: And in fish brine - Which is made from the innards of fish, and all the more so [is he permitted] in muryas [fish gravy], which is made only from the fat of fish.

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:4:4.english: He is prohibited from fish brine and fish gravy - For these are included in [the category of] minced [sardines].

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:7:1.hebrew: הלך אחר לשון בני אדם - שקורין דג לגדול ודגה לקטנים. להכי, כי אמר דג, מותר בקטנים; וכי אמר דגה, אסור בקטנים; וכי אמר דג דגה, אסור בשניהם:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:7:1.english: Follow the language of people - For [people] call a large [fish] dag, and small [fish] daga. Therefore, when he says dag, he is permitted [regarding] small [fish]; and when he says daga, he is forbidden [regarding] small [fish]; and when he says dag daga, he is forbidden [regarding] both of them.

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:8:1.hebrew: אמר הרי עלי ציחין - מי אמר דמדגים ממש קאמר ולא מדבר אחר, או דילמא דמי כמאן דאמר מן הצחנה:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:8:1.english: [If] he said: "Tziḥin are hereby [forbidden] to me" - Do we say that he means actual fish and not something else, or perhaps it is like one who says, "[I vow] from tzaḥana"?

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:9:1.hebrew: מן הקום - משג"א, היינו נסיובי דחלבא, דקום אינו בכלל חלב:
Rashi on Nedarim 51b:9:1.english: From whey [kum] - [In Old French:] mesgue, that is, whey [nesiovei dechalava], for kum is not included in [the category of] milk.

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:9:2.english: Prohibits - Because he holds that there is a trace of milk in it, and it is included in [the category of] milk.

Rashi on Nedarim 51b:9:3.english: [One who vows] from whey is permitted milk - [This is] the opinion of all, for milk is not included in whey.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:1:1.hebrew: קונם מן הכבוש - שאמר "קונם כבוש עלי", אינו אסור אלא בכבוש של ירק, דסתם כבוש משמע כבוש של ירק, אבל לא "כבוש שאני טועם" — כיון שאמר "שאני טועם", אסור בכל הכבושים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:1:1.english: Konam from pickled food - [Where] he said, "Konam, pickled food [is forbidden] to me," he is prohibited only from pickled vegetables, for unqualified "pickled food" implies pickled vegetables; however, [this is] not [the case with] "pickled food that I taste" — since he said "that I taste," he is prohibited from all pickled foods.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:1:2.english: "From the boiled [food]" - Without specification, it refers to [boiled] vegetables.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:2:1.hebrew: דכבוש מאי - פירוש: אם אמר "קונם דכבוש עלי", מאי? כסתם "כבוש" דמי, ואינו אסור אלא בכבוש ירק, או דילמא כ"שאני טועם" דמי, ואסור בכל הכבושי':
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:2:1.english: "That which is pickled, what [is the halakha]?" - Explanation: If one said, "Konam [is] that which is pickled upon me," what [is the halakha]? Is it like an unspecified [vow mentioning] "pickled," so that he is prohibited only from pickled vegetables, or perhaps it is like [saying] "that I taste," so that he is prohibited from all pickled foods?

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:3:1.english: "From the roasted [food]" - Unspecified, it is [roasted] meat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:3:2.english: "From salted food" - Unspecified "salted food" is salted fish.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:1.hebrew: דג דגים שאני טועם - פירוש: דג או דגים. ורבי שמעון, דאמר בגמרא "דג" גדולים משמע, פליג אהא; וי"א: דג ודגים, דאמר לתרוייהו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:1.english: "Fish, fishes that I taste" - Explanation: [It means] "fish" [singular] or "fishes" [plural]. And Rabbi Shimon, who says in the Gemara [that] "fish" [singular] implies large ones, disagrees with this. And some say: [It means] "fish and fishes," where he said both of them.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:2.hebrew: בטרית טרופה - מין דג גדול שחותכין וטורפין אותו, ולא מיקרי לא דג ולא דגים, אלא יש להם שם בפני עצמם:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:2.english: [He is permitted] tarit terufah - [This is] a type of large fish that they cut and beat, and it is called neither "fish" nor "fishes," rather they have a name of their own:

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:3.hebrew: טרית - טונינ"א בלע"ז. וי"מ שלכך מותר בטרית, שלא נתכוון אלא בדגים שלמים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:3.english: Tarit - Tonine [tuna] in the vernacular. And some explain that the reason he is permitted [to eat] tarit is because he intended [to prohibit] only whole fish.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:4.hebrew: ומותר בציר - אע"פ שדגים מעורבין בו, וא"צ לומר מורייס, שאין בו אלא שומן דגים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:4.english: And he is permitted fish brine - Even though fish are mixed into it, and needless to say muryas [fish gravy], which contains only fish fat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:5.hebrew: הנודר מן הצחנה - דגים טרופים, כדאמר בע"ז (דף מ -) ובסנהדרין (דף מ: '): "מוניני וצחנתא טעים ופריס להו". וי"מ: דגים קטנים, ולפי שהטרית חתוכה בחתיכות קטנות הוי בכלל צחנה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:5.english: One who vows [to abstain] from tzaḥana - [This refers to] minced fish, as [the Gemara] says in Avodah Zarah (40a) and in Sanhedrin (40b): "Munini and tzaḥanta, one tastes [them] and breaks them apart." And some explain: [they are] small fish, and because the sardine is cut into small pieces, it is included in [the category of] tzaḥana.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:6.hebrew: ומותר בציר ובמורייס - דאין ניכר בהם ממשות הדגים, ולא נתכוון אלא לממשות הדגים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:6.english: And he is permitted fish brine and fish gravy [morays] - For the substance of the fish is not recognizable in them, and he only intended [to prohibit] the substance of the fish.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:7.hebrew: הנודר בטרית טרופה אסור בציר ובמורייס - טרופה, ואין טרופה גדולה מזה, שאין בהם רק ליחלוחית הדג ושומנו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:4:7.english: One who vows [against] minced sardines is prohibited from fish brine and fish gravy - [It is] minced, and there is nothing more minced than this, for they contain only the moisture of the fish and its fat.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:5:1.hebrew: תניא ר' שמעון אומר דג שאני טועם אסור בדג גדול - דדג משמע דג גדול, כדכתיב: "וימן ה' דג גדול":
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:5:1.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon says: "[If one says:] 'Dag that I taste,' he is prohibited from [eating] a large fish" - For dag implies a large fish, as it is written: "And the Lord appointed a great fish" [Jonah 2:1].

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:5:2.hebrew: דג דגה - פירוש: שאמר שניהן; בין גדולין בין קטנים — משמע מייתור הלשון:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:5:2.english: Dag dagah - Explanation: [This means] that he said both [terms]; [that he is prohibited from] both large and small [fish] is implied from the redundancy of the phrasing.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:7:1.english: "In the belly of the dagah," etc., "with regard to vows, follow the language of people" - And [people] call small [fish] dagah.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:8:1.hebrew: הרי עלי צחיחין - כיון דאמר לשון זה, משמע צחנתא זו דוקא ומותר בטרית טרופה, או דלמא כנודר מן הצחנה ואסור בטרית:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:8:1.english: Tzeḥiḥin are hereby [forbidden] to me - Since he said this expression, [does it] imply specifically this tzaḥanta, and he is permitted [to eat] minced sardines (terit terufah), or perhaps [it is] like one who vows [to abstain] from tzaḥana, and he is forbidden [to eat] sardines?

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:1.hebrew: ומותר בקום - מי חלב, דהואיל ופסולת חלב הוא — אינו בכלל חלב. ורבי יוסי אוסר, דפסולת חלב הוי בכלל חלב:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:1.english: And he is permitted [to partake of] whey [kum] - [That is,] milk water, for since it is the waste product of milk, it is not included in [the category of] milk. But Rabbi Yosei prohibits [it], for the waste product of milk is included in [the category of] milk.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:2.hebrew: קום - מי חלב שקורין משג"א. ורבי יוסי סבר דקום בכלל חלב, וכן חלב בכלל קום. וי"מ: הנודר בקום מותר בחלב לדברי הכל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:2.english: Kum - Milk-water [i.e., whey] that is called mesgue [in Old French]. And Rabbi Yosei holds that kum is included in [the category of] milk, and likewise milk is included in [the category of] kum. And some explain: One who vows [that] kum [is forbidden to him] is permitted [to partake] of milk according to all opinions.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:3.hebrew: הנודר מן הגבינה אסור בין מלוחה בין תפילה - ואע"ג דלא אכלי אינשי אלא מלוחה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:3.english: One who vows [not to benefit] from cheese is prohibited [from it], whether salted or unsalted - Even though people only eat [it] salted.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:4.hebrew: הנודר מן הבשר מותר ברוטב ובקיפה - אע"ג שיש בו טעם בשר, ואע"ג דקיפה הוי בשר שנקפה בשולי הקדירה — דלא קרי אינשי בשר אלא חתיכות בשר שהן בעין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:4.english: One who vows [not to benefit] from meat is permitted [to partake] of gravy and of sediment [kifah] - Even though it [the gravy] has the taste of meat, and even though kifah is meat that congealed at the bottom of the pot — because people do not call [anything] "meat" except pieces of meat that are intact.

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:5.english: Rabbi Yehuda prohibits [them] - Because he holds [that] it and its flavor [are treated alike].

Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:6.hebrew: בבשר מותר ברוטב - לכאורה משמע דמותר בשר להחליף ולמכור, וכן בנודר מן הענבים ומן התאנים, שאינו מתכוין לאסור עצמו בהנאת מין כשהוא מזכיר; אבל כשאמר "קונם בשר זה עלי" — אסור אפילו בהנאה, וכי ההיא ד"קונם פירות הללו עלי" דאסור בחילופיהן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 51b:9:6.english: [He is prohibited] in meat, [and] permitted in gravy - At first glance, it implies that the meat is permitted to be exchanged and sold, and similarly in the case of one who vows [to abstain] from grapes or from figs, for he does not intend to forbid himself from deriving benefit from a species when he mentions [it generally]. However, when he says, "Konam, this meat [is forbidden] to me," it is forbidden even for [other] benefit, like that [teaching] of "Konam, these fruits [are forbidden] to me," where he is forbidden [to benefit] from their exchanges.
